itinerary.cal: Best attempted July-September once brush has dried out and snow has cleared from the upper talus and summit gully.

days.note: From the Eagle Creek/Beckler River road-end, climbers push through huckleberry brush to a streambed, cross talus around 4,000 ft, then work up heathered slopes and granite steps to a talus basin below the summit block. Since the true east ridge crest is unsuitable for direct travel, most parties detour through the basin and scramble the class 3-4 col from the north ridge to reach the top; morning fog often lingers into mid-morning.
days.title: East Ridge scramble, car to car

schedule.label: Leave Seattle
schedule.detail: ~1.5-2 hr drive to Baring via US-2, then Beckler River Rd/NF-6514-410 to road's end.

schedule.label: Start hiking
schedule.detail: Trailless start; push through huckleberry brush toward a brushy streambed.

schedule.label: Cross talus at ~4,000 ft
schedule.detail: Route-find across talus and heathered slopes, avoiding dense slide alder.

schedule.label: Reach talus basin below summit block
schedule.detail: Fog can linger here past 10 AM in some seasons; wait out clouds if needed.

schedule.label: Summit via north ridge col
schedule.detail: Class 3-4 scramble up the bouldered east summit; helmet recommended for loose rock.

schedule.label: Back at road-end
schedule.detail: Descend by mostly retracing the ascent line, correcting around brushy sections.

days.objective: Summit via the north ridge/talus basin col and return same day

itinerary.totalNote: A long single day: about 8-10 hrs car-to-car, roughly 3,400 ft gain over 4.8 miles round trip, done entirely off-trail.
